blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: A pool task's run() calls drainQueue(), which loops `while (!Thread.interrupted()) { process(queue.poll()); }`. When drainQueue() returns, run() does `if (Thread.currentThread().isInterrupted()) return;` and otherwise schedules the next drain. The pool is shut down with shutdownNow() while drainQueue() is processing. What does run() do?

options.text: It reaches its check and returns, since the request is still set when drainQueue() ends
options.says: Thread.interrupted() reads the flag and clears it, so the request is gone by the time run() checks

options.text: It reaches its check and schedules another drain, since drainQueue() cleared the request on its way out
options.says: the inner loop saw the request through Thread.interrupted(), which cleared it; the caller's isInterrupted() then finds nothing

options.text: It never reaches its check, since shutdownNow() ends the pool's thread as soon as it is called
options.says: interrupt() only sets a flag; the thread runs on until its own code checks

options.text: It never reaches its check, since the loop in drainQueue() keeps running after the shutdown
options.says: the loop does check, with Thread.interrupted(), so it ends after the item in progress

origin.section: Interrupting a Thread Sets a Flag, and Running Code Stops Only Where It Looks

questions.stem: A consumer runs `while (!Thread.currentThread().isInterrupted()) { try { Event e = events.poll(2, SECONDS); if (e != null) handle(e); } catch (InterruptedException ex) { log.warn("poll interrupted"); } }`. Its owner calls interrupt() once, while the consumer is inside poll(). What follows?

options.text: The loop ends at its next check, since the flag was still set when poll() threw
options.says: a blocking call that throws InterruptedException clears the flag first, so the check reads false

options.text: The loop goes on polling, since the flag was cleared when poll() threw
options.says: the exception carried the request and cleared the flag; the catch only logged it, so the loop condition never sees it

options.text: The consumer stays in poll() until the two seconds are up, since a timed poll() returns at its timeout and not on an interrupt
options.says: an interrupt ends a blocking call such as poll() at once, with InterruptedException

options.text: The consumer stays in poll() until an event arrives, since a waiting poll() returns on an event and not on an interrupt
options.says: an interrupt ends a blocking call such as poll() at once, with InterruptedException

origin.section: A Blocking Call Answers by Throwing, and the Throw Clears the Flag

questions.stem: A report thread is interrupted while it computes totals in a loop that never looks at the flag. When the loop is done, the thread calls Thread.sleep(500) before writing the file. What happens at the sleep?

options.text: It throws InterruptedException at once, since the flag set during the computation is still set when sleep() begins
options.says: nothing read or cleared the flag, and a blocking call made with the flag set throws at once

options.text: It throws InterruptedException at once, since sleep() checks whether the thread was interrupted at any point before
options.says: sleep() looks at the flag as it is now; a thread whose earlier interrupt was already cleared sleeps normally

options.text: It lasts the full 500 ms, since the flag set during the computation was cleared when that loop ended
options.says: nothing cleared the flag: a loop that never looks at it leaves it set

options.text: It lasts the full 500 ms, since sleep() checks for interrupts that arrive while it waits, not before it
options.says: a waiting method also throws when the thread is already interrupted as it enters

origin.section: A Blocking Call Answers by Throwing, and the Throw Clears the Flag

questions.stem: A pricing job runs `while (!stopped) { recalculate(nextSku()); }`, where stopped is a volatile field that the job's stop() method sets. On a deploy, the job's pool is shut down with shutdownNow(). What happens to the job?

options.text: It stops after the current SKU, since shutdownNow() asks each running job to stop through its stop() method
options.says: shutdownNow() knows nothing of the job's methods or fields; it interrupts the pool's threads

options.text: It stops after the current SKU, since shutdownNow() interrupts the thread, which ends a loop over a volatile field
options.says: an interrupt sets the thread's flag; it does not touch the job's field, and the loop reads only the field

options.text: It goes on recalculating, since shutdownNow() interrupts the thread, which a loop over that field never notices
options.says: shutdownNow() interrupts the pool's threads, which sets the interrupt flag and not the job's field, and the loop never checks the flag

options.text: It goes on recalculating, since shutdownNow() leaves running jobs alone and only drops the queued ones
options.says: shutdownNow() interrupts running tasks as well as returning the queued ones

origin.section: Interrupting a Thread Sets a Flag, and Running Code Stops Only Where It Looks

concepts: A thread whose flag is already set gets InterruptedException at once from its next wait.
A cancellation field of the task's own is never set by shutdownNow() or Future.cancel, which set the interrupt flag.
A blocking call answers an interrupt by throwing InterruptedException and clears the flag, so a catch that carries on loses the request.
